Tom Brady.text: Taken 199th overall in the sixth round of the 2000 draft, earning a reputation as the NFL's biggest draft steal.
Tom Brady.evidence: After playing college football for the Michigan Wolverines, Brady was selected 199th overall by the Patriots in the sixth round of the 2000 NFL draft, later earning him a reputation as the NFL's biggest draft steal.

Drew Brees.text: Led the league in passing yards a record seven times.
Drew Brees.evidence: He also led the league in passing yards a record seven times.

Peyton Manning.text: Ended his career by winning Super Bowl 50, the first starting quarterback to win it with two franchises.
Peyton Manning.evidence: Manning's career ended with a victory in Super Bowl 50, making him the first starting quarterback to win the Super Bowl for more than one franchise.

Brett Favre.text: Started 297 consecutive regular season games, the most in league history.
Brett Favre.evidence: Favre had 321 consecutive starts from 1992 to 2010, including 297 regular season games, the most in league history.

Aaron Rodgers.text: The first quarterback ever to post a regular-season career passer rating over 100.
Aaron Rodgers.evidence: Apart from a regular-season career passer rating of over 100 (the first to ever have a career rating over 100), he also holds the best touchdown-to-interception ratio and the lowest passing interception percentage in NFL history while also having had the highest passer rating in NFL history throughout the entire 2010s decade.

Matthew Stafford.text: The fastest player in NFL history to reach 40,000 career passing yards.
Matthew Stafford.evidence: He is currently sixth all time in passing yards per game and the fastest player in NFL history to have reached 40,000 career passing yards.

Ben Roethlisberger.text: Did not play quarterback in high school until his senior year, giving way to the coach's son.
Ben Roethlisberger.evidence: At Findlay High School in Findlay, Ohio, Roethlisberger was captain of the Trojans' football, basketball, and baseball teams. Roethlisberger did not play quarterback until his senior year, giving way to the coach's son, Ryan Hite.

Philip Rivers.text: After four years away from the NFL, he re-signed with the Colts near the end of the 2025 season.
Philip Rivers.evidence: Following four years away from the NFL, Rivers re-signed with the Colts near the end of the 2025 season, where he played his final three games.

Matt Ryan.text: After retiring as a player, he rejoined the Falcons in 2026 as their president of football.
Matt Ryan.evidence: After retiring, he rejoined the Falcons in 2026 as the president of football.

Dan Marino.text: The last quarterback taken in the first round of the famed quarterback class of 1983.
Dan Marino.evidence: Marino was the last quarterback taken in the first round of the famed quarterback class of 1983.
